review.publication: Local only. No commit, push or deployment.
review.scope: Animal feeding roles versus mammalian taxonomy; hunting activities and human roles; catching versus successful capture; traps and bait; inherited fish-species targets; pursuit and protection.
review.attribution: Reviewed adaptations of Open English WordNet 2025 by the Open English WordNet Team, derived from Princeton WordNet; CC BY 4.0 and Princeton notices remain in docs/quality/2026-10-09-q11.md#sources-and-reuse. NCBI, Idaho Fish and Game and the National Park Service support biological distinctions. Russian labels and graph mappings are editorial adaptations; source prose is not copied.
review.context_policy: All additions use U1 and unspecified strength. Preserve old home contexts, explicit negations, reviewed fishing genera and valid mammal ancestry. Ecological roles and taxonomic membership are separate axes.

sense_decisions.scope: An animal belonging to the mammalian order Carnivora, regardless of whether its usual food is meat or plants.
An animal in the prey role of predation, not a human victim or a captured quantity.
The biological interaction in which an animal kills and eats another animal; exclude plundering and metaphorical exploitation.
Intersection of predatory and prey roles in a food web, without requiring the same counterparty or time.
A bird that preys on other animals; a functional group, not a single avian order.
A fish that preys on other animals; not every fish and not a mammal.
An animal whose diet is chiefly animal flesh; neither membership in Carnivora nor personally killing every food animal is required.
An animal able to obtain nutrition from both plant and animal matter; this is a feeding category.
Consumption of plant material by an animal; distinguish obtaining food from supplying food to another animal.
Dead and decaying animal remains; not a living animal or a manufactured artifact.
Consumption of dead animal remains; distinguish it from killing live prey and from collecting discarded objects.
The carrion-feeding restriction of the broader dictionary scavenger meaning; exclude chemical scavengers and people collecting discarded objects.
Intersection of predation and carrion feeding; neither feeding strategy excludes the other.
The human-performed restriction of the existing hunting activity, without guaranteed success or a commercial motive.
Hunting undertaken for recreation; no licensing rule or legal classification is asserted.
Hunting for livelihood through obtaining animal products; distinguish this purpose from recreation.
Hunting for the hunter or household to obtain food; not necessarily commercial.
A hunter whose hunting is work or livelihood.
A person participating in recreational hunting; not disjoint from being an occupational hunter in another setting.
The animal-targeted restriction of physical catching, without guaranteed capture.
The successful taking of an animal, not merely a fishing or hunting attempt.
Catching activity using traps; excludes horse trappings and figurative entrapment.
Human hunting by animal-trapping methods; not all animal trapping is hunting.
A human hunter using traps; no automatic worker genus or compulsory fur target.
Fishing specifically targeting the named fish group; the restriction is independent of gear, location and livelihood.
Fishing specifically targeting the named fish group; the restriction is independent of gear, location and livelihood.
Fishing specifically targeting the named fish group; the restriction is independent of gear, location and livelihood.
Fishing specifically targeting the named fish group; the restriction is independent of gear, location and livelihood.
Fishing specifically targeting the named fish group; the restriction is independent of gear, location and livelihood.
Fishing specifically targeting the named fish group; the restriction is independent of gear, location and livelihood.
A manufactured device intended to catch an animal; excludes plumbing, golf and figurative traps.
An animal trap intended to retain the animal alive, without asserting every deployment is harmless.
Luring with an animal as its target; no guaranteed capture or harm.
Material used to attract an animal; may be natural or manufactured, so the dictionary device genus is not imposed.
Animal bait used to attract fish; includes natural bait and manufactured lures.
A living animal used as bait; not a manufactured device.
Fishing bait supplied by a living animal.
Use the ecological predator meaning, not the taxonomic order.
Reuse the Russian herbivore record instead of making an English duplicate.
The person role is broader than a worker; the dictionary occupational genus is narrowed into a separate intersection.
Keep successful capture distinct from attempting to catch.
Reuse the physical catching activity without infection, perception or baseball senses.
Reuse attraction as an action; create a separate animal-targeted restriction.
Preserve the existing explicit negative hunting assertion without extending it to every non-predatory activity.
Defer the mixed physical/mental catch meaning instead of merging by a shared English spelling.
The dictionary noun trapping denotes horse covering; use the animal-trapping verb sense instead.

review.limits: No general hunt implies successful capture, killing or eating. No food-web class is equated with a taxonomic order, and predator/prey roles are not disjoint. Existing probabilistic animal capabilities and the non-predator negation are retained without recalibration. Fox/fox synonyms, bear/panda taxonomy, protection subtypes, physical versus mental catch senses and additional malformed aliases remain queued. Dictionary trapping (horse covering) and poaching (cooking) are not imported into hunting.

exclusion_review.decision: Preserve clear scans, upper exclusions and explicit negations. Reject only the specifically reviewed hunting/protection coordinate assertion.

review.collision_decision: Reuse existing Russian hunter, herbivore, catching, luring and pursuit concepts. No new normalized-term collisions accepted.

refreshed_comparison.caveat: Spelling candidates are not verified identities or missing-concept counts.
